Review Lab

A 1,400-line pull request adds the tournament interface. It hides 4 architecture problems, 4 bugs and 6 style issues. Choose how big the change is when it's reviewed, what checks style, in which order reviewers read, and whether they use a checklist, then see what's found and what reaches players.

One change, three reviewers. Goal: no architecture problem and no bug merged, with at most 4 hours of review.

Lesson 070: reviewing code as an architect

    What this shows

    Attention is the budget

    Every comment about a brace is attention not spent on a hot path. Let tools own style, and reviewers own meaning.

    Big changes hide big problems

    Reviewers find far less per line in a 1,400-line change than in a 350-line one. Split by meaning: interface first, then each implementation.

    Read from the outside in

    Design problems live in interfaces, dependencies, hot paths and failure modes, not in any one line. Start there, with five questions, before reading the details.

    This lab is a model, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 070's numbers: 4 architecture problems, 4 bugs and 6 style issues in 1,400 lines. Reviewers find 1 bug in one big PR and 3 in four small ones, plus 1 more when tools take style off their plate. Line by line finds 0 architecture problems in the big PR and 1 in small ones; reading outside in finds 2; with the checklist, 4. Human style review adds 60 comments and 1.5 hours. Review time: 3 hours for the big PR, 2.5 for four small ones, +0.5 for the checklist. A missed bug costs 8 hours after merge; a missed architecture problem 40.
